unit.unitOverview: Say what you can do and what you can't do. Ask: Can you swim? Say what you like, love and hate: I like cooking. Join two things with and.
unit.learningPath:
The lesson: listen and repeat.
Words: listen, look and say. 26 words.
Patterns: 3 cards. Read the one done for you.
Reading: read the 3 texts. Say them.
Speaking: tap the mic. Say it. Listen.
Writing: write about you. Made-up answers are OK.
Practice: write. Check with the answers.
Quiz: 12 questions. Last, My progress.

visual.lectureScript:
Hello! This is Unit 4.
In this unit, you say what you can do.
And you say what you like.
Listen.
I can cook. I can drive.
I can't swim.
Can: yes. Can't: no.
Can't and cannot are the same.
After can, the word stays the same.
I can swim. Not: I can swimming.
He can sing. She can dance. Can has no s.
Now a question.
Can you swim?
Yes, I can. No, I can't.
Listen to can and can't.
Can is short. Can't is long.
I can swim. I can't swim.
Now like.
I like music.
I like cooking.
After like, add -ing: cook, cooking.
Love: like it very, very much. I love dancing.
Don't like is no. I don't like running.
Hate is no, not at all. I hate running.
Look at dancing. Dance ends in e. Drop the e.
Look at running and swimming. Two n. Two m.
Now and.
And is for two things.
Music and films.
I can cook and I can drive.
Three things? I can sing, dance and draw.
After like, both words take -ing.
I like cooking and swimming.
Now you. Say one thing you can do.
Say one thing you like.
It can be true or made up.
Now go to Words. Goodbye!

grammar.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 3, Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 3
grammar.title: Can and can't: I can swim, I can't drive
grammar.explanation:
Can: yes. I can cook.
Can't: no. I can't drive.
Can't and cannot are the same.
After can, the word stays the same.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
I can swim.
You can drive.
He can cook.
She can sing.
We can dance.
They can run.

I can't swim.
She can't drive.

Can you swim?
Yes, I can.
No, I can't.

He can, she can: no s.
Not: he cans.
grammar.workedExample:
Sam: swim, yes. Drive, no.
1. Swim, yes: can.
2. Sam can swim.
3. Drive, no: can't.
4. Sam can't drive.
5. Check: swim and drive stay the same. Yes.
grammar.commonMistake:
It is easy to add to or -ing after can.
No: I can to swim.
No: I can swimming.
Yes: I can swim.
grammar.memoryTip: Can, then the word as it is.
grammar.practice:
Write can or can't.
1. Lena: cook, yes. Lena ___ cook.
2. Ivan: drive, no. Ivan ___ drive.
3. Zoe: swim, yes. Zoe ___ swim.
4. Yara: sing, no. Yara ___ sing.
5. Tomas: ride a bike, yes. Tomas ___ ride a bike.
6. Mia: draw, no. Mia ___ draw.
7. ___ you swim? Yes, I can.
8. Can you drive? No, I ___.
grammar.answerKey:
1. can  2. can't  3. can  4. can't  5. can  6. can't  7. Can  8. can't
Wrong on 7? A question starts with Can: Can you swim?
Wrong on 8? No goes with can't: No, I can't.

grammar.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 3, Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 3
grammar.title: Like with -ing: I like singing
grammar.explanation:
Say what you like and do not like.
Use like, love, don't like or hate.
Then a thing, or a word with -ing.
I like music. I like cooking.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
I love dancing.
I like cooking.
I don't like running.
I hate carrying bags.

a thing: I like music.
a word with -ing: I like singing.

Make the -ing word:
cook, cooking
sing, singing
carry, carrying

An e at the end? Drop the e.
dance, dancing
drive, driving
ride, riding

swim, swimming: two m
run, running: two n
grammar.workedExample:
Dance: yes, very, very much. Write a line.
1. Very, very much: love.
2. After love: a word with -ing.
3. Dance has an e at the end. Drop the e.
4. dance, dancing.
5. Write: I love dancing.
6. Check: no e before -ing. Yes.
grammar.commonMistake:
It is easy to leave out -ing after like.
No: I like cook.
Yes: I like cooking.
No: I like swiming.
Yes: I like swimming. Two m.
grammar.practice:
Write the word with -ing.
1. I like ___. (cook)
2. I love ___. (dance)
3. I don't like ___. (run)
4. I hate ___ bags. (carry)
5. I like ___. (sing)
6. I love ___. (swim)
7. I don't like ___. (drive)
8. I like ___. (draw)
grammar.answerKey:
1. cooking  2. dancing  3. running  4. carrying  5. singing  6. swimming  7. driving  8. drawing
Wrong on 2 or 7? Dance and drive end in e. Drop the e.
Wrong on 3 or 6? Run and swim take two letters: running, swimming.

grammar.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 3, Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 3
grammar.title: And: sing and dance
grammar.explanation:
Use and for two things.
Two words: music and films.
Two parts: I can cook and I can drive.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
Two words:
Ana and Sam
music and films
sing and dance

Two parts:
I can cook and I can drive.
I like music and I love dancing.

Or say can one time:
I can cook and drive.

Three things? A comma, then and:
I can sing, dance and draw.

After like, both words take -ing:
I like cooking and swimming.
After can, no -ing:
I can cook and swim.
grammar.workedExample:
I can sing. I can dance.
Make one sentence.
1. Two lines, both with I can.
2. Put and in the middle.
3. I can sing and I can dance.
4. Or: I can sing and dance.
5. One full stop, at the end.
grammar.commonMistake:
It is easy to drop -ing after and.
No: I like cooking and swim.
Yes: I like cooking and swimming.
After can, no -ing at all.
No: I can sing and dancing.
Yes: I can sing and dance.
grammar.memoryTip: Two things, one and, one full stop.
grammar.practice:
Make one sentence with and.
1. I can cook. I can drive.
2. I like music. I like films.
3. Ana can swim. Sam can swim.
4. I love singing. I love dancing.
5. I can't swim. I can't drive.
6. I can walk. I can run. I can ride a bike.
grammar.answerKey:
1. I can cook and I can drive. Or: I can cook and drive.
2. I like music and films. Or: I like music and I like films.
3. Ana and Sam can swim.
4. I love singing and dancing. Or: I love singing and I love dancing.
5. I can't swim and I can't drive.
6. I can walk, run and ride a bike.
Wrong on 6? Three things: a comma, then and.
Wrong on 4? After love, both words take -ing.

writing.title: Writing 2 — What I like
writing.promptAndInstructions:
Write 4 lines with love, like, don't like and hate.
Put a word with -ing in each line.
They can be true or made up.
writing.modelText:
I love dancing.
I like cooking.
I don't like running.
I hate driving.
writing.successCriteria:
4 lines: love, like, don't like, hate.
A word with -ing in each line.
Spelling: dancing has no e. Swimming has two m. Running has two n.
writing.support:
Copy the model.
Change the -ing word only.
Check each one with the list in Pattern 2.

writing.title: Writing 3 — Two things with and
writing.promptAndInstructions:
Write 4 lines about you with and.
In 2 lines, join two words.
In 2 lines, join two parts with I can or I like.
writing.modelText:
I like music and films.
I can sing and dance.
I can cook and I can drive.
I like walking and I love swimming.
writing.successCriteria:
4 lines, each with and.
One full stop in each line, at the end.
After like and love: -ing on both words.
writing.support:

Now put and between them.
I can sing and I can dance.
writing.extension: Write one line with three things: I can sing, dance and draw.

writing.title: Writing 4 — A card for a group

activities.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 3, Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 3
activities.title: Practice 1 — Can or can't
activities.instructionsAndItems:
Read. Then write can or can't.
Priya: cook, yes. Drive, yes. Swim, no. Sing, no.
Tomas: swim, yes. Dance, yes. Cook, no. Drive, no.
1. Priya ___ cook.
2. Priya ___ swim.
3. Tomas ___ swim.
4. Tomas ___ drive.
5. Priya ___ drive.
6. Tomas ___ cook.
7. Tomas ___ dance.
8. Priya ___ sing.
activities.answerSummary:
1. can  2. can't  3. can  4. can't  5. can  6. can't  7. can  8. can't
Check 2 and 3: swim is no for Priya and yes for Tomas.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 1 and do it again.
activities.soloPath: Write your answers on paper. Check with the key. Count the right ones.

activities.title: Practice 2 — Add -ing
activities.instructionsAndItems:

2. swim

activities.answerSummary:
1. cooking  2. swimming  3. dancing  4. walking  5. running  6. riding  7. playing  8. sleeping  9. carrying  10. speaking
The hard ones: 2 and 5 (two m, two n), 3 and 6 (drop the e).
9 or 10 right: good.

activities.title: Practice 3 — Can swim, like swimming
activities.instructionsAndItems:
Write the right word.
1. I can (swim / swimming).
2. I like (cook / cooking).
3. I can't (drive / driving).
4. I love (dance / dancing).
5. Can you (sing / singing)?
6. I don't like (run / running).
7. I hate (carry / carrying) bags.
8. I can (ride / riding) a bike.
activities.answerSummary:
1. swim  2. cooking  3. drive  4. dancing  5. sing  6. running  7. carrying  8. ride
The rule: can and can't, no -ing. Like, love, don't like and hate, -ing.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Patterns 1 and 2 and do it again.
activities.soloPath: Say each line out loud with your word. Write the word. Check with the key.

activities.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 3, Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 3
activities.title: Practice 4 — Join with and
activities.instructionsAndItems:
Make one line with and.
1. I can swim. I can run.
2. I like football. I like music.
3. Ana can cook. Lena can cook.
4. I love singing. I love dancing.
5. I can draw. I can count to twenty.
6. I like films. I like songs. I like games.
activities.answerSummary:
1. I can swim and I can run. Or: I can swim and run.
2. I like football and music. Or: I like football and I like music.
3. Ana and Lena can cook.
4. I love singing and dancing. Or: I love singing and I love dancing.
5. I can draw and I can count to twenty. Or: I can draw and count to twenty.
6. I like films, songs and games.
Wrong on 6? Three things: a comma, then and.
5 or 6 right: good.
4 or less: read Pattern 3 and do it again.
activities.soloPath: Write each line. Read it out loud. Check with the key. Both answers count where the key gives two.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Make the sentence
activities.instructionsAndItems:
Make a sentence.
Start with a capital letter.
End with a full stop or ?
1. can / I / swim
2. like / I / cooking
3. you / can / drive
4. don't / I / running / like
5. and / sing / I / dance / can
6. is / favourite / my / football / game
7. can / speak / Yara / two languages
activities.answerSummary:
1. I can swim.
2. I like cooking.
3. Can you drive?
4. I don't like running.
5. I can sing and dance.

Number 6: Football is my favourite game. That is right too.

assignments.title: I can, I like
assignments.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Tap the mic. Say hello and your name. Say two things you can do and one thing you can't do. Say two things you like, with and. Say goodbye.
2. Write a group card like Writing 4.
You can use a made-up name. Your answers can be made up.

teacherNotes.note: Every card shows one item done before its practice, every exercise has a key with a score line, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back and a short checklist. If you are helping, listen to the recordings together and point at the checklist rather than correcting mid-sentence.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 3, Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 3
teacherNotes.noteType: The one error worth your attention
teacherNotes.note: The two patterns meet in this unit, so they swap: I can swimming, I like cook. Practice 3 sets them side by side on purpose. When you hear one, point at the word before the verb, can or like, and let the learner fix the verb themselves. The tip line is the whole rule: can swim, like swimming.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 3, Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 3
teacherNotes.note: No task asks whether the learner can really swim, drive or ride a bike. Every I can task lets them pick or invent, and a made-up answer practises the language exactly as well as a true one. Driving in particular depends on age and on where a person lives; never ask, and never correct a made-up answer.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 3, Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 3
teacherNotes.note: I don't like is used as one chunk with like. Questions and short answers with do, and short forms such as don't and isn't, are Unit 7, so do not explain do here. Every question here is built with can or with is, so none needs do. He likes, with its s, is also left for later: this unit keeps like to I, you, we and they, and teaches only that can has no s. Joining with but, or and then is Unit 13.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 3, Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 3
teacherNotes.note: The AI tutor is a rehearsal partner, not a marking service, and no task is scored by it alone. The learner is told throughout that a made-up name and made-up answers are fine. Keep that wording, and never ask the learner to give the tutor real personal details.
